projects.name: Project Description | The PaymentService project enables seamless integration with the Worldpay payment gateway to facilitate secure and efficient transactions for FX-related operations. The service exposes four key APIs:
details: CreateToken
Authorize (Auth)
Reauthorize (Reauth)
FetchTransaction
These APIs allow customers to add funds to their wallet or virtual account, which is a mandatory step before performing any FX transaction.

A merchant code-based configuration is implemented to ensure secure and controlled transaction processing. Each merchant code must be explicitly enabled in Worldpay before being activated in the PaymentService system. This two-step activation ensures only authorized merchant codes are used for transactions.

To support various upstream channels, the system is configured to use separate merchant codes for web, mobile, and offline platforms, allowing precise tracking and categorization of business transactions

entry.text: Project Description | Services Hub is a telecom-based product offering a complete mobile repair management solution. It is currently used by T-Mobile Austria for both in-store (shop users) and end-customer scenarios. The platform integrates with multiple external systems to manage the full mobile repair lifecycle seamlessly.
Key integrations include:
URLS (Universal Reverse Logistics System): Handles the actual mobile device repair process.
Viveum Payment Gateway: Facilitates secure payment transactions for repair services within the Services Hub.
Key Features and Functionalities:
Case creation for customer-reported mobile defects.
Collection of customer and device-related defect information.
Box Management: Enables shop users to prepare a single shipment box for multiple devices.
Support for DOA (Dead on Arrival) case handling.
Upload and management of purchase receipts.
Loaner Pool Management: Allows shop users to lend temporary replacement devices to customers.
Real-time notifications (email/SMS) sent to customers and shop users for each status update or action performed via URLS, Viveum, or within the Services Hub itself.

projects.name: Project Description | The SmartyStreets Service is a Spring Boot-based microservice designed to perform address validation using the SmartyStreets API. This service acts as a middleware component between the Evavi Application and the external SmartyStreets API.
details: Request Handling: Evavi sends address validation requests to the SmartyStreets Service.
External API Integration: The service calls the SmartyStreets API with the provided address data.
Response Transformation: Upon receiving the JSON response from SmartyStreets, the service processes and converts it into a predefined XML format.
Response Delivery: The XML-formatted address validation response is returned back to the Evavi Application.
This architecture ensures encapsulation of third-party API logic within the service and provides a stable, formatted interface to the Evavi Application.

projects.name: Project Description | The PaymentService project enables seamless integration with the Worldpay payment gateway to facilitate secure and efficient transactions for FX-related operations. The service exposes four key APIs:
details: CreateToken
Authorize (Auth)
Reauthorize (Reauth)
FetchTransaction
These APIs allow customers to add funds to their wallet or virtual account, which is a mandatory step before performing any FX transaction.

A merchant code-based configuration is implemented to ensure secure and controlled transaction processing. Each merchant code must be explicitly enabled in Worldpay before being activated in the PaymentService system. This two-step activation ensures only authorized merchant codes are used for transactions.

To support various upstream channels, the system is configured to use separate merchant codes for web, mobile, and offline platforms, allowing precise tracking and categorization of business transactions

Support for DOA (Dead on Arrival) case handling.

entry.text: Project Description | Services Hub is a telecom-based product offering a complete mobile repair management solution. It is currently used by T-Mobile Austria for both in-store (shop users) and end-customer scenarios. The platform integrates with multiple external systems to manage the full mobile repair lifecycle seamlessly.
Key integrations include:
URLS (Universal Reverse Logistics System): Handles the actual mobile device repair process.
Viveum Payment Gateway: Facilitates secure payment transactions for repair services within the Services Hub.
Key Features and Functionalities:
Case creation for customer-reported mobile defects.
Collection of customer and device-related defect information.
Box Management: Enables shop users to prepare a single shipment box for multiple devices.
Support for DOA (Dead on Arrival) case handling.
Upload and management of purchase receipts.
Loaner Pool Management: Allows shop users to lend temporary replacement devices to customers.
Real-time notifications (email/SMS) sent to customers and shop users for each status update or action performed via URLS, Viveum, or within the Services Hub itself.
Roles & Responsibilities: | Understood the client's business processes to ensure that technical solutions align with functional requirements.
Participated in daily team meetings, discussions, and agile ceremonies to track progress and address blockers.
Involved in coding and development of server-side components using Spring, Hibernate, and RESTful web services.
Contributed to daily build processes and ensured code stability through continuous integration.
Participated in QA, UAT, and Production deployments, ensuring smooth transition across environments.
Provided production support, including issue resolution, system monitoring, and root cause analysis.

projects.name: Project Description | The SmartyStreets Service is a Spring Boot-based microservice designed to perform address validation using the SmartyStreets API. This service acts as a middleware component between the Evavi Application and the external SmartyStreets API.
details: Request Handling: Evavi sends address validation requests to the SmartyStreets Service.
External API Integration: The service calls the SmartyStreets API with the provided address data.
Response Transformation: Upon receiving the JSON response from SmartyStreets, the service processes and converts it into a predefined XML format.
Response Delivery: The XML-formatted address validation response is returned back to the Evavi Application.
This architecture ensures encapsulation of third-party API logic within the service and provides a stable, formatted interface to the Evavi Application.
